answers.why: Israel's outcasts are gathered as the LORD rebuilds Jerusalem.
Israel receives statutes and judgments in contrast to other nations in the next verse.
Israel parallels the children of Zion rejoicing in their King.
The Preacher rules over Israel as king in Jerusalem.
Israel is the nation supplying the warriors who surround Solomon's bed.
Judah and Jerusalem are the subjects of Isaiah's vision during the reigns of Judah's kings.
Israel is explicitly paralleled with God's people who do not understand.
The sinful nation has provoked its God, the Holy One of Israel.
The mighty One of Israel announces judgment against the community with rebellious princes.
Isaiah's prophecy concerns Judah together with Jerusalem.
Judah and Jerusalem lose their supplies of bread and water and their leaders.
Judah falls alongside Jerusalem because their speech and deeds oppose the LORD.
